Journal of Glaciology 43(143), 98–102. doi:10.3189/S0022143000002859. Bibliographic discovery only; original unavailable.
sources.actual_read_scope: Bibliographic discovery metadata only. The sole exact normal publisher-article open returned a completed web-reader timeout. No original article body, map pixels or figure was acquired or used.
sources.source_identity: Discovery identified an original university satellite-change analysis in its own journal issue, comparing 1993 Landsat analysis with digitized 1961 photogrammetric topography. This independently issued research article was distinguished from the stopped Ives 1962 article figure, GSC geological reports, CanMatrix distribution and PP1386 atlas. The potential underlying topographic base was not treated as newly acquired cartographic evidence.
sources.limits: Discovery snippets, parsed labels and descriptions of unseen figures are not substantive selected-route evidence. The independent publication identity does not imply geographic coverage or successful acquisition.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and upper south-to-north/east approach
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening and most of its northward/eastward upper route lie west of the 90-degree-west neatline of P.3626, and outside the lower-corridor coverage of P.3625. Neither map establishes this initial channel, possible waterbody passages or its continuous connection to the later mapped route. No nearby river or lake name is transferred to this interval.
correspondence.correspondence: Material geographic gap; opening and upper connectors unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Short east-of-neatline middle loop
correspondence.finding: P.3626 depicts a sinuous channel entering its western edge, running north close to that edge, and leaving west again. Its bends and side-waterbody arrangement correspond at corridor scale to the short selected east-of-90-degree-west loop. The larger lakes farther east are separate from this selected channel and are not assigned as selected lake passages. The source does not display a clear name for this small mapped interval.
correspondence.correspondence: Only the short on-sheet interval is supported; its upstream and downstream off-sheet continuations remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Intervening western and north-eastern connector to the lower mapped corridor
correspondence.finding: After the short mapped loop, the selected path returns west of P.3626 and subsequently turns northeast beyond that sheet’s northern edge. P.3625 starts farther east, at 89 degrees 35 minutes west, leaving a substantial interval between the two inspected pieces. The sources therefore do not establish a continuous through-link from the chosen opening to the mapped lower Nettle corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Material geographic gap; the maps cannot be joined into complete selected-route coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: Western entry to P.3625 and lower northeast-going reach
correspondence.finding: At P.3625’s western edge, the selected east-going reach corresponds to the labelled Nettle River. Its sequence of bends continues northeast and then north. The map distinguishes the East Nettle River joining from the south/east; that tributary label is not assigned to the selected western incoming mainstem.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported from the selected western entry into this sheet through the lower northeast-going bend and tributary setting.

correspondence.component_scope: North-going lower river and lateral tributary pattern
correspondence.finding: The selected course follows the north-going channel carrying another direct Nettle River label. Its broad bends and lateral channel/pond pattern agree with the mapped river. Tiskran River and other west-side tributary or creek entries, and Milk Creek to the east, remain distinct side components; no side-branch name is substituted for the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary lower-corridor and junction scale, without assigning every local branch or floodplain pond.

correspondence.component_scope: Branched coastal approach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: P.3625 shows the selected northern approach continuing along Nettle River into its branched mouth on Hudson Bay. Nearby separately labelled Katawi Creek, Kanistik River and Sakatawon River lie west of this outlet and are distinct. The actual selected sea-class ending corresponds to the Nettle River–Hudson Bay coastal outlet, not to a neighbouring creek or an inland lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at river-to-bay and coastal-mouth scale; precise present shoreline, tide state and individual mouth-branch boundary are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and first hook
correspondence.finding: The selection begins west of the Chila de Juárez/Honey corridor, bends south and then turns northeast toward the mapped Las Marías approach. Honey depicts Las Marías but does not establish the selected western hook as a connected stream. The generalized state mapping shows separate intermittent approaches without settling that chosen through-link. Tenango’s municipal footprint does not supply the missing southern connection. No river identity is inferred from basin membership or neighboring labels.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Marías–Cuarco–San Marcos upper passage
correspondence.finding: Honey labels Las Marías on its northeast-running river. Pahuatlán maps the western entry with Las Marías and Cuarco labels, a distinct southern joining approach near its urban corridor, and the continuing San Marcos reach. The selected eastward route corresponds to this western approach, without assigning the separate southern tributary or the northern Acalman branch to the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Tlacuilotepec–San Pedro Petlacotla and Villa Ávila Camacho joins
correspondence.finding: The state original shows the upper corridor passing the Tlacuilotepec/Ozomatlán setting, turning northeast past San Lorenzo and San Pedro Petlacotla, and continuing along the directly labeled San Marcos reach. The Clima watercourse joins from the south near Villa Ávila Camacho; the selected approach is the western one. The northern Pantepec drainage is separate.

correspondence.component_scope: San Marcos middle bends to Poza Rica
correspondence.finding: Readable originals show the San Marcos corridor east toward Villa Lázaro Cárdenas, the southern bend by San Bartolo del Escobal, then the northeast/east return toward El Vizcaíno, Zacate Colorado and the Coatzintla/Poza Rica reach. The selected bends and intervening joins match at ordinary generalized corridor scale. Nearby southern drainages are not substituted for this route.

correspondence.component_scope: Poza Rica to Cazones lower river
correspondence.finding: The selected line follows the river along the western side of Poza Rica and northeast toward La Concepción and Cazones de Herrera. The municipal Relieve original directly labels Cazones on the lower river, and its hydrography table independently lists Cazones as a corriente de agua. Candidate naming therefore does not depend on the settlement name or basin label.

correspondence.component_scope: Expanded lower fluvial waterbody, coastal bends and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The broad lower meandering waterbody is directly labeled Cazones and remains part of the river corridor. Its large southward loop and northern coastal turn lead to the direct Gulf of Mexico opening at Barra de Cazones. La Boquilla and the separate neighboring estuarine/coastal waters are not the selected ending. No selected lake, reservoir or managed canal passage is established on the observed corridor; no modern shore or precise mouth vertex is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and first downstream bend
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening follows the mapped southward drainage beside the Pedro Alexandre–Nossa Senhora da Glória boundary sector, passing the settlement area shown near PA Fortaleza. The watercourse then bends east into the corridor labelled Rio Sergipe. Monte Alegre provides the full opening and turn; the Carira original overlaps the northern approach and labels its downstream continuation. The initial point is an arbitrary selected opening, not a claim to the river’s ultimate spring or a precisely delimited name-change point.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward Rio Sergipe and northern Carira corridor
correspondence.finding: The connected river runs east past the Cipó-de-Leite vicinity and across the northern Carira boundary corridor. Direct Rio Sergipe labels occur on the channel. The mapped mouth of Riacho Melancia and other local lateral streams joins this trunk; those feeders are distinguished from the selected eastward continuation. The overlap with Aparecida shows the same river entering its successive southeastern bends.

correspondence.component_scope: Aparecida bends and turn toward Feira Nova
correspondence.finding: The selected river follows the continuous sinuous northern Aparecida boundary, including the repeated southward loops and eastern continuation. The Aparecida and Feira Nova map frames overlap geographically, exposing the river’s transition into the western Feira Nova corridor. This is a connected channel comparison, not inference from a municipality or basin label. Side drainage and nearby water shapes are not substituted for the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Feira Nova–São Miguel do Aleixo corridor
correspondence.finding: The Feira Nova original shows the main river along the municipality’s western margin, then the longer southeastward and southern bends beside São Miguel do Aleixo. Lateral streams enter from both sides and the selected route remains on the continuous named Rio Sergipe corridor. The southern map portion overlaps the Dores original and establishes the transition into the next reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Rio Sergipe through the Dores area
correspondence.finding: The Dores original shows the connected river from the upper western boundary into the interior west of the town, past successive junctions and then south/southeast toward Santa Rosa de Lima. The river continues after it leaves the orange municipal-boundary line; it is followed as blue mapped drainage rather than treating that administrative line as a watercourse. No selected large reservoir or separately named lake through-passage is shown in this reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Rosa connection and Riachuelo reach
correspondence.finding: The Santa Rosa original supplies overlapping coverage on both sides of the intervening map-frame interval. It shows the river coming from the Dores area, turning southeast to Santa Rosa de Lima and then south/southwest before entering the Riachuelo map. The Riachuelo original shows the continuing river and the eastward lower turn past the town, with a direct Rio Sergipe label and mapped lateral joins. The western Jacarecica waterbody/branch setting on the broader Riachuelo sheet is separate from the selected upstream approach; no reservoir traversal is inferred from its proximity.

correspondence.component_scope: Riachuelo–Maruim narrow-to-broad transition
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Riachuelo, Maruim and Socorro originals show the selected river continuing south from Riachuelo, bending near João Gomes de Melo, broadening into the lower river and then turning east and southeast. The Maruim map resolves the whole connection and the north-side tributary entry independently of the Riachuelo legend area. Repeated Rio Sergipe labels occur along the connected trunk. The wide mapped water is a continuation of the estuarine river, not a named lake or a reservoir assumed from its width.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower estuary and tributary/channel junctions
correspondence.finding: The Socorro original follows the broad Rio Sergipe southeast from the Maruim overlap, past the western Cotinguiba entry and the Rio do Sal junction, then south toward Aracaju. It distinguishes the selected main estuary from the lateral branches and the Canal Pomonga connection on the eastern side. The mapped connected water and overlapping Aracaju view support the through-route without requiring an unsupported basin-level inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal and Atlantic connection
correspondence.finding: The Aracaju original shows the lower Rio Sergipe estuary between Aracaju and Barra dos Coqueiros, with the Poxim-side western branching/water area kept distinct from the selected main passage. The selected downstream end lies in the lower estuary/mouth sector. The original visibly continues that estuarine water through the coastal opening into the labelled Oceano Atlântico. The retained modeled sea-terminal classification is therefore described through its actual estuarine setting; neither an exact present shoreline intersection nor a precise ocean-mouth vertex is assigned. The nearby Vaza-Barris coastal outlet farther south is a different system and is not substituted.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern headward opening and initial southwest descent
correspondence.finding: The selected fragment begins in the northeast and descends southwest before turning west. No allowed original map was inspected that establishes the actual opening, its local channel, any source lake or glacier association, or its connection into the long upper corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Long upper westward corridor and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues broadly west through a sequence of model links and shallow bends. The original cartographic evidence needed to distinguish river reaches from possible lake, ice-margin or other connecting intervals was not acquired. The model links alone do not establish continuous natural drainage or material junctions.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northward return and southwest continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected line makes a shallow northward return, then turns southwest. Its actual intermediate through-connections, adjoining branches, waterbody passages and local component names remain unestablished at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward and southwestward corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues west and southwest toward the coastal sector. No allowed original map establishes the chosen lower river, any lake outlet or branch transfer, and the continuous link from the middle route to the terminal approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southern approach and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected approach trends south and southwest. Neither the actual receiving bay or marine waterbody nor its connection to the selected lower route has been established from allowed primary cartography. A modeled coastal classification is not substituted for inspection of the actual terminal.
